correctness.rationale: An independent integer census (python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence-5.py with NumPy) constructed both transition maps by squaring residues modulo 13, applying the stated synchronous update, and iterating nested full images. At the first equality of consecutive image sizes the restrictions are a finite permutation, so the image is precisely the recurrent set and that iteration is the sharp maximum entry time. Walking the cycles of this image and following all unresolved initial states until first entry yields the primitive cycle counts (1,2288,6), recurrent populations (1,6864,78), basin totals (1498799,88114,7410), six individual 13-basins of size 1235, and sharp depth 14 attained by 624 states at threshold two. Since the least common multiple of the periods is 39 and depth-14 states are not yet periodic at time 13, F_2^53=F_2^14 but F_2^52≠F_2^13. The independent transition map sends 0000002221110 to its translate by +3, and for each affine image with multiplier a the speed is 3a; these are the six distinct quadratic residues. The 78 affine images are distinct and equal the independently enumerated period-13 set. At threshold three the stabilized image is just zero, at time four, with 101062 states first entering at that time. The frozen transcript and its two inspected classifier algorithms are consistent with these independently obtained results.
